title: Activation-balanced INT8 profile orchestration and kernel compatibility matrix
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Goal: implement an activation-balanced INT8 quantization orchestration that produces deterministic per-model quant profiles, integrates into the calibration pipeline, and exposes a runtime kernel compatibility matrix so the serving runtime can choose safe fallback paths with minimal accuracy regression. This ticket covers: (1) profile generation algorithm that computes per-tensor rescale factors using activation statistics stratified by token position and layer type, (2) calibration harness adjustments to collect representative prefix distributions and per-batch max/percentile signals, (3) generation of a kernel compatibility manifest (CPU/GPU/accelerator variants) and tagging model artifacts with required runtime flags, (4) end-to-end validation against our evaluation harness with accuracy/latency/cost trade-off reports, and (5) pragmatic rollout controls (canary policy, automatic fallback to FP16/FP32 kernels when thresholds fail).

This differs from earlier activation-aware efforts by: focusing on "activation-balanced" profiles (explicit per-block scale scheduling), recording deterministic metadata for runtime kernel selection, and adding a compact compatibility matrix consumed at deploy-time to avoid surprise failures when kernels are missing or quant modes differ across infra variants.
acceptance_criteria: Produce deterministic INT8 quant profiles for 3 canonical LLMs (7B/13B/70B) using the new activation-balanced algorithm
Calibration harness collects per-layer 99.9th percentile and histogram sketches for activations and stores them with the profile artifact
Runtime kernel compatibility manifest generated for CUDA kernels (smoothed scaling), Triton fallback paths, and CPU reference kernels; manifest format documented
Accuracy regression <= 1% relative to baseline FP16 on standard prompt suite for each model and workload type
End-to-end deploy: model with profile + manifest can be deployed to Dedicated and Hosted with automatic safe-fallback behavior verified in canary
Documentation updated: profile schema, runtime flags, and deploy checklist present in Confluence (link in links)
tasks: Design and document activation-balanced profile schema and metadata fields (author: Aisha)
Extend calibration worker to emit per-batch activation histograms and percentile summaries (engineer: Marcus)
Implement profile generator that merges statistics across shards and computes per-block rescale schedule (engineer: Marcus)
Add exporter to tag model artifacts with compatibility manifest and signed hash (engineer: S. Gomez)
Implement runtime manifest ingestion and kernel selection logic in serving runtime (engineer: runtime team)
Create evaluation runs (PR: github.com/redwood/quant-eval PR#2345) and record accuracy/latency/cost metrics
Create canary rollout job and validate fallback behavior under simulated missing-kernel scenarios
Write docs, example CLI commands, and a lightweight tutorial for SEs
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting — agreed on profile fields and stored artifacts. Decided to use 99.9th percentile + histogram sketch (t-digest) to capture heavy tails.
2026-03-02: Prototype calibration worker emits histograms to S3; tested on 7B model with 10K prompts; initial profiles produced but showed 2.3% QA regression on chat-clamp prompts.
2026-03-04: Algorithm tweak — introduced per-block multiplier damping (0.8–1.0) to avoid over-scaling activation sneak peaks; regression dropped to 0.6% on same suite.
2026-03-05: Generated kernel compatibility manifest format v1.0 and instrumented the model export to include signed manifest. Began runtime integration PR.
Notes: calibration runs are slow for 70B; need to add prioritized sampling and early-stopping heuristics for long tails.
review_comments: PM review (Jordan Park): Ensure the canary rollback policy is explicit — if any model’s per-prompt perplexity delta > 1.5% we must pause and require manual approval.
Design input (Lina Chen): Add a visual diff export for deviation heatmaps so SEs can quickly see which layers contribute most to regression.
Security (R. Patel): manifest signing approach ok but include KMS key id and rotation metadata in manifest header
Runtime lead (Ethan Nguyen): prefer manifest to include "kernel_families" field to avoid adding ad-hoc flags later; will review PR #4572
qa_plan: Unit tests for profile serializer/deserializer and manifest signature verification
Integration tests: calibration worker -> profile generator -> runtime manifest ingestion (CI job)
Regression suite: run standard 1.2K prompt set plus adversarial clamp prompts; fail build if accuracy regression > 1%
Performance tests: measure per-token latency overhead when enabling per-batch rescale hooks; target < 7% p50 overhead
Chaos test: deploy to canary with kernel intentionally omitted to validate automatic fallback to FP16 path
perf_targets: Accuracy regression threshold: <= 1% relative to FP16 baseline on standard suite
p50 latency overhead (serving): <= 7% with INT8 rescale enabled
p99 latency SLO: no more than 25ms regression on 13B-class models for 16-token responses
Calibration cost: reduce sample count with prioritized sampling to keep calibration compute under 0.6x of current baseline for 70B
notes: Trade-off: tighter percentile (99.99) reduces edge-case regressions but increases quant scale and token-level error in low-latency workloads — we'll expose percentile knob in profile schema
Follow-up: add FP8 probe lanes later if activation-balanced profiles prove robust; keep schema forward-compatible
Operational: include a telemetry flag when a model uses activation-balanced profile so Console can show per-route cost deltas
Fallback policy: if manifest indicates missing kernel family, runtime should attempt binary-compatible kernel, else fall back to FP16 with safety holdoff and alert
